item.title: Spa bliss in the Alps: hot springs and hiking in the shadow of Mont Blanc
item.description:
Source: The Guardian Travel Pre-analysis score: 0.84
An autumn break in the French mountain town of Saint-Gervais-Les-Bains offers thermal treatments and glorious walking trails before the winter ski crowds descend Mont Blanc is hiding behind the clouds, but the Aiguille du Midi spears the sky above a mountainside ablaze with russet, gold and tawny tones. The maples flare red; rowan trees are dusted with crimson berries. Our little group has trundled up to Mont Lachat station (altitude: 2,115 metres) on the Tramway du Mont Blanc, the century-old cog railway that climbs improbably steep slopes from the French alpine town of Saint-Gervais-les-Bains. Operational since 1909, the railway was once intended to reach the 4,809-metre summit of Mont Blanc, but war, glacial terrain and waning funds put an end to that ambition. But even from Mont Lachat, the view is a showstopper. On one side, the Bionnassay Glacier slips scenically down the slope, a buzzard soaring over the milky-green glacial lake at its base, while on the other the Chamonix valley basks in soft autumnal sunshine. item.title: Understanding Giardia: Causes, Symptoms, and the 24-Hour Power of Tinidazole
item.description:
Source: Sectionhiker.com Pre-analysis score: 0.84
An outdoor adventure can occasionally be disrupted by an invisible microscopic threat. This threat is Giardia duodenalis (also known as Giardia lamblia or Giardia intestinalis), a tiny protozoan parasite responsible for giardiasis, one of the most common waterborne intestinal infections worldwide.
